description: Where this board's build finds its tools, and nothing else. Replaces the
old workflow config file, whose remaining live content was one key - the
path to kicad-cli - alongside configuration for a router this project no
Linux-native. KiCad is the distribution package, so kicad-cli and the
stock libraries sit on the system prefix and `pcbnew` imports from the
system interpreter's dist-packages - there is no separate bundled Python
to find. `cli` and `python` are bare command names on purpose: they
resolve through PATH, which keeps a fresh clone working on any machine
that has the packages, and the resolved absolute path is recorded in the
run's own provenance rather than frozen here.
Design rules, net classes, via sizes and clearances are deliberately NOT
restated here. They live in the .kicad_pro net classes, which is the same
source the generator, the router and the validator all read.

router.name: KiCad Routing Tools
router.note: Resolved through pcbqa.krt: explicit override, then this development checkout, then a single active plugin installation; a path under disabled_pcm_plugins always refuses. The old PCM-rooted 'root' key is retired - that installation is disabled on purpose. On Linux the KiCad user base is ~/.local/share/kicad, so the plugin directory is versioned beneath it. That directory need not exist: nothing has been installed there, the scan skips a directory that is absent, and on this machine it is development_checkout that resolves. It is listed so that an installed plugin WOULD be found, and so that the disabled_pcm_plugins refusal has somewhere to apply.

toolkit.note: The pinned submodule. Board tools add this to sys.path through tools/_toolkit.py; no sibling checkout is ever used.
